title: Chapter 2 Quiz: Foundations of Machine Learning
description: Test your knowledge of Supervised vs Unsupervised learning, preprocessing, regression, and model evaluation metrics.

questions.question: In which machine learning paradigm are training examples paired with ground-truth target labels (X, y)?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning relies on explicit input-output label pairs to learn the mapping function.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of Unsupervised Learning?
options: Discovering underlying structure, patterns, or clusters in unlabeled data
questions.explanation: Unsupervised learning extracts latent structures, groupings, or representations without external labels.

questions.question: Reinforcement Learning agents learn optimal behaviors by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative reward.
questions.explanation: True. Reinforcement learning is driven by state observation, action execution, and reward feedback.

questions.question: Predicting whether an email is 'Spam' or 'Not Spam' is an example of which task?
questions.explanation: Predicting one of two discrete classes is binary classification.

questions.question: Predicting the continuous market selling price of a car based on mileage and age is:
questions.explanation: Regression models predict numerical continuous scalar values.

questions.question: Which preprocessing technique converts categorical variables without ordinal ranking into binary dummy columns?
questions.explanation: One-Hot Encoding creates a new binary 0/1 column for each discrete nominal category.

questions.question: What is the mathematical range of Min-Max Normalization: (x - x_min) / (x_max - x_min)?
questions.explanation: Min-Max scaling compresses values strictly into the interval [0, 1].

questions.question: Standardization (Z-score scaling) transforms a feature to have a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1.
questions.explanation: True. Z = (x - mean) / std centers the distribution at 0 with unit variance.

questions.question: What is the primary loss function minimized in ordinary Linear Regression?
questions.explanation: Linear regression minimizes the average squared differences between true and predicted values (MSE).

questions.question: What non-linear function is applied to the linear combination z = w*x + b in Logistic Regression to bound outputs between 0 and 1?
questions.explanation: The Sigmoid function 1 / (1 + e^-z) maps real-valued numbers into probabilities between 0 and 1.

questions.question: When a machine learning model fits training data perfectly by memorizing noise but fails on unseen test data, it suffers from:
questions.explanation: High variance (overfitting) occurs when a complex model captures training noise rather than true generalizable patterns.

questions.question: A model that is too simple to capture the underlying pattern in data suffers from High Bias (Underfitting).
questions.explanation: True. High bias represents strong erroneous assumptions that cause the model to miss underlying trends.

questions.question: Why is evaluating a model solely on raw accuracy misleading when working with highly imbalanced datasets?
options: A trivial model predicting only the majority class can yield high accuracy while missing all minority cases
questions.explanation: On a dataset with 99% negative samples, predicting 'negative' every time achieves 99% accuracy while detecting 0% of positives.

questions.question: Which evaluation metric measures the ratio of True Positives out of all Predicted Positives (TP / (TP + FP))?
questions.explanation: Precision measures how many of the positively predicted instances were actually correct.

questions.question: Which metric measures the proportion of actual positive cases successfully caught by the model (TP / (TP + FN))?
questions.explanation: Recall measures the model's ability to identify all relevant ground-truth positive instances.

questions.question: The ______ score is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall.
questions.explanation: The F1-score balances precision and recall into a single unified metric: 2 * (P * R) / (P + R).

questions.question: In K-Fold Cross Validation, the dataset is split into K equal subsets, training K separate times with each fold serving as validation once.
questions.explanation: True. K-Fold provides a comprehensive generalization estimate by rotating the validation fold across all data.

questions.question: What is data leakage in machine learning pipelines?
options: RAM memory leaking into swap space
Information from the test set inadvertently contaminating the training process
questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when validation/test signals leak into training, artificially inflating performance estimates.

questions.question: If a hospital needs an AI diagnostic system that minimizes the risk of missing any cancerous tumor, which metric should be maximized?
questions.explanation: High recall minimizes false negatives, ensuring critical cases (like malignant tumors) are not missed.

questions.question: The validation set should be used to tune model hyperparameters, while the test set is reserved exclusively for final evaluation.
questions.explanation: True. Keeping the test set untouched prevents hyperparameter tuning bias.
